title: Amram the Dyer
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Gittin 52b relates that he was a guardian of orphans and came before Rav Nachman. His name is not otherwise known among the sages, according to Hyman.[^1][^2]

notes.text: נב: gives Gittin 52b by the colon convention. The separately read Davidson paragraph explicitly names Rav Nachman, supporting that ר״נ expansion in this exact Amram/guardianship episode. It says the relatives came before him, whereas Hyman’s compressed wording is translated with Amram as implicit subject; the difference is preserved, not harmonized. Hyman’s unknown-among-sages observation is not a fresh exhaustive search.
צבעא is the lexical occupational epithet the Dyer; it does not add a personal rabbinic title or certify an authority identity.
